Read all the way through the request path — the generated API interface, the controller, the mapper, the normalizer utilities, and the service. Here is everything that happens, in order, when you `POST /api/owners`.

## 1. Before the controller method runs

**a. Authorization** — `@PreAuthorize("hasRole(@roles.OWNER_ADMIN)")` on `addOwner`. The caller must hold the `OWNER_ADMIN` role or the call is rejected (403) before any body processing.

**b. Bean Validation of the request body** — the generated `OwnersApi.addOwner` declares `@Valid @RequestBody OwnerFieldsDto`, so all constraints on `OwnerFieldsDto` are enforced (a violation → 400, before the controller body executes):
- `firstName` — `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..30)`, `@Pattern(^[\p{L}]+([ '-][\p{L}]+){0,2}$)` (letters, up to three words separated by space/apostrophe/hyphen).
- `lastName` — `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..30)`, `@Pattern(...\.?$)` (same as first name but an optional trailing `.` is allowed).
- `address` — `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..255)`, `@Pattern(.*\S.*)` (must contain a non-whitespace char).
- `city` — `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..80)`, `@Pattern(.*\S.*)`.
- `telephone` — `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..20)`, **plus the custom `@TelephoneDigits`** — which passes only if `TelephoneNormalizer.toE164(telephone)` yields a value (i.e. after stripping spaces/dashes/brackets it forms `+` and 8–15 digits, assuming `+61` and dropping a leading `0` when no `+` is given). Null telephone passes this custom check but is caught by `@NotNull`.
- `email` — `@Email` and `@Size(max 255)`; optional (nullable).
- `registrationDate` — `@Valid`, optional.
- `sharesHousehold` — no constraints; defaults to `false`.

## 2. In the controller (`addOwner`)

**c. Map DTO → `Owner`** via `ownerMapper.toOwner(ownerFieldsDto)`, which applies these transformations (side-effects on the new entity):
- `id` and `pets` are ignored (not set).
- `address` is normalized by `AddressNormalizer.normalize` — trimmed, internal whitespace collapsed to single spaces, upper-cased, and street-type abbreviations expanded (`ST`→`STREET`, `RD`→`ROAD`, `AVE`→`AVENUE`).
- `telephone` is normalized to E.164 by `TelephoneNormalizer.toE164(...).orElse(null)`.
- `email` is lower-cased by `EmailNormalizer.normalize` (`Locale.ROOT`).
- `firstName`, `lastName`, `city`, `registrationDate` are copied through as-is.

**d. Compute `sharesHousehold`** — `Boolean.TRUE.equals(ownerFieldsDto.getSharesHousehold())` (a null flag becomes `false`). It is passed to the service but never stored on the owner.

## 3. In the service (`createOwner`, `@Transactional`) — in this exact order

**e. Duplicate-telephone check** — if `ownerRepository.existsByTelephone(owner.getTelephone())`, throw `DuplicateTelephoneException`.

**f. Household lookup + duplicate-household check** — `findHouseholdMembers` finds existing owners with the same last name (case-insensitive) and the same address after `TextNormalizer.normalize`. If any exist **and** `sharesHousehold` is false, throw `DuplicateHouseholdException`.

**g. City-capacity check** — `ownersInCity = countByCity(city)`; if `>= MAX_OWNERS_PER_CITY` (50), throw `CityCapacityExceededException`.

**h. Registration-date defaulting + business-day adjustment** *(side-effect)* — if `registrationDate` is null, use `LocalDate.now()`; then set it to `BusinessDayAdjuster.toBusinessDay(...)` (a Saturday/Sunday rolls forward to the next Monday; weekdays unchanged).

**i. Daily-limit check** — `ownersOnDate = countByRegistrationDate(adjusted date)`; if `>= MAX_OWNERS_PER_DAY` (100), throw `DailyOwnerLimitExceededException`.

**j. Namesake count** *(side-effect)* — `owner.setNamesakeCount(countNamesakes(owner))`, counting existing owners sharing the same first + last name (case-insensitive).

**k. Customer code** *(side-effect)* — `owner.setCustomerCode(CustomerCodeGenerator.format(city, lastName, ownersInCity + 1))`.

**l. Household join** *(side-effect, conditional)* — if household members exist, `owner.setHouseholdId(joinHousehold(...))`, which generates a shared `HouseholdIdGenerator` id and **also re-saves each existing member** whose household id differs.

**m. Persist** — `ownerRepository.save(owner)`; the method returns the resulting `householdId`.

## 4. Back in the controller (response)

**n.** Map the saved `Owner` back to `OwnerDto` (`toOwnerDto`, which also computes derived fields: `displayName`, `initials`, `membershipNumber`, `membershipTier`, `locality`), set the `Location` header to `/api/owners/{id}`, and return **201 Created**.

Note that the checks in step 3 execute sequentially and short-circuit — the first one that fails throws and aborts, so, e.g., the city-capacity check is only reached after the telephone and household checks pass.
